QuestionStmt.S: If $3 \sin 2\theta = 2 \sin 3\theta$ and $0 < \theta < \pi$, then the value of $\sin \theta$ is equal to

Solution.S:
Given: $3 \sin 2\theta = 2 \sin 3\theta$.

Using $\sin 2\theta = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta$ and $\sin 3\theta = 3\sin\theta - 4\sin^3\theta$:

$$3(2\sin\theta\cos\theta) = 2(3\sin\theta - 4\sin^3\theta)$$

$$6\sin\theta\cos\theta = 6\sin\theta - 8\sin^3\theta$$

Dividing by $\sin\theta$ (since $\theta \neq 0$):

$$6\cos\theta = 6 - 8\sin^2\theta$$

$$6\cos\theta = 6 - 8(1 - \cos^2\theta)$$

$$6\cos\theta = 6 - 8 + 8\cos^2\theta$$

$$8\cos^2\theta - 6\cos\theta - 2 = 0$$

$$4\cos^2\theta - 3\cos\theta - 1 = 0$$

$$(\cos\theta - 1)(4\cos\theta + 1) = 0$$

$$\cos\theta = 1 \quad \text{or} \quad \cos\theta = -\frac{1}{4}$$

Since $0 < \theta < \pi$, $\cos\theta \neq 1$. Thus $\cos\theta = -\frac{1}{4}$.

$$\sin^2\theta = 1 - \cos^2\theta = 1 - \frac{1}{16} = \frac{15}{16}$$

$$\sin\theta = \frac{\sqrt{15}}{4}$$

Hence the correct option is D: $\frac{\sqrt{15}}{4}$.
